targets.why_hot: Building a cut-manifest index appends every line offset as a Python int, then copies that list into a uint64 array in _write_index. On 200000 JSONL records the traced peak is 11231304 bytes and is the live list of ints; the .idx file itself is only the compact uint64 vector plus a size sentinel. Writing the offsets straight into a pre-sized uint64 buffer would leave those bytes unchanged and drop the Python-int list from the peak.

targets.why_hot: One merge of a 400-turn session allocates 2568 objects, and most of them are not the merged supervision. The custom and alignment key unions call dict.keys() on every turn, which builds a view and an iterator per dict, to rediscover a handful of repeated names. The overlap-warning scan also copies sups[1:] and recomputes SupervisionSegment.end (a freshly rounded float) on both sides of every adjacent pair. The alignment concat itself is already one copy plus extend. Dropping the key views, the neighbor-list copy, and the duplicate end values still returns an equal MonoCut, leaves the input cut unchanged, and keeps the merged word list distinct from each source list.

targets.why_hot: JSONL with no class hint is fully parsed into a list of dicts so RecordingSet, SupervisionSet, FeatureSet, and CutSet can be tried in order. The successful CutSet is constructed while that list is still referenced, so peak traced memory holds every raw dict and every cut at once (4329686 bytes for 1500 cuts). Releasing each dict after its cut is built, or sniffing the type from the first record the way load_manifest_lazy already does, returns an equal manifest and cuts that peak. Type selection and the ValueError paths covered by the native tests have to stay the same.

targets.why_hot: JsonMixin.to_json materializes list(self.to_dicts()) and then json.dumps it with indent=2. Cut.to_dict calls asdict_nonull, and dataclasses.asdict deep-copies every nested dataclass, list, and dict. On a 1500-cut manifest that is 428349 object allocations per call, while two calls write identical bytes and the in-memory CutSet is left unchanged. Emitting that same document by walking fields, without the deep copy, keeps the file bytes and the cut objects the same.
